contribution_after.assessment: Building on Davis et al. (2024) and Stroebl et al. (2024), the paper frames verifier-limited resampling through attainable sets, finite-compute odds-ratio thresholds (Proposition 2), a covariance identity separating pooled precision from the abstaining ceiling plus a mean-preserving spread ordering (Proposition 3 and Rothschild & Stiglitz 1970), and candidate re-verification under correlated verdicts (Proposition 4, untested). The expanded empirical study covers 40 main HMMT problems and 25 harder Omni-MATH problems on frozen outputs, but remains small, leaves most main-set check differences unresolved from zero and the harder-set self-check gain (+0.022) non-significant, and documents substantial benchmark memorization (>=30% and >=67% explicit recall in the stronger model's verdicts), leaving the overall contribution as a useful synthesis.

new_problems.evidence: In simulation/pc/estimators.py lines 104-164 and simulation/run_all.py lines 124-135, protocol curves switch from without-replacement permutations/U-statistics over the m=6 observed attempts (n <= 6) to i.i.d. with-replacement plug-in curves from the 6-attempt empirical distribution (n >= 7). Recomputing across n=1..8 gives a downward step at n=6 -> n=7 on the newly added robustness run (Oracle and Stronger model drop from 0.720000 to 0.706128, Plurality vote from 0.680000 to 0.638562, Agreement from 0.652444 to 0.629274) and on the main set (Vote drops from 0.925000 to 0.915219, and Agreement—newly changed to permutations up to n=6—drops from 0.922222 to 0.913093). Although paper/PAPER.md line 106 and figure captions disclose switching to plug-in beyond 6, Section 5.5 line 164 comments only on the self-check curve turning down (due to item r04) without noting why Oracle and other monotone protocols dip visually at n=7 in Figure 3b.
